Other Minor Shareholders (29%) | num_employees = 59,756 (2025) | website = {{URL|jdplc.com}} | footnotes = }} '''JD Sports Fashion plc''', commonly known as '''JD Sports''', '''JD''' or '''JD Group'''{{cite web|url=http://www.lslav.co.uk/Projectsjdsports.html|title=New distribution warehouse, Rochdale|access-date=28 February 2020}} is a British multinational sports-[[fashion]] retail company based in [[Bury, Greater Manchester]], England. It is listed on the [[London Stock Exchange]] and is a constituent of the [[FTSE 100 Index]]. The [[Pentland Group]] owns 55% of the company.{{cite web|url=https://www.drapersonline.com/news/pentland-sells-177m-stake-in-jd-sports|title=Pentland sells £177m stake in JD Sports|date=12 December 2019|publisher=Drapers Online|access-date=14 February 2022}} The company operates mainly in Europe, North America and Asia-Pacific.{{Cite web |url=https://jdplc.com |title=Business Overview |publisher=JD Sports Fashion PLC |access-date=6 April 2026}} ==History== The company was established by John Wardle and David Makin (hence the name ''JD''), trading from a single shop in [[Bury, Greater Manchester]], in 1981.{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/business/news/jd-sports-founder-sells-11per-cent-stake-to-firm-behind-speedo-552365.html |title=JD Sports founder sells 11per cent stake to firm behind Speedo|work=The Daily Telegraph|date=7 July 2004 | location=London | first=Rachel | last=Stevenson|access-date=28 February 2020}} The company opened a store in the [[Arndale Centre]] in [[Manchester]] in 1983. [[Pentland Group]] bought Wardle's and Makin's shares for £44.6M in May 2005,{{cite news|url=http://business.timesonline.co.uk/tol/business/industry_sectors/retailing/article521191.ece|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110612020354/http://business.timesonline.co.uk/tol/business/industry_sectors/retailing/article521191.ece|url-status=dead|archive-date=12 June 2011|title=JD Sports founders sell out for £44.6m|publisher=Times Online|date=5 November 2007 | location=London}} so acquiring 45% of the business.{{cite news |last=Finch |first=Julia |title=JD Sports founders cash in and quit with £45m |newspaper=[[The Guardian]] |date=12 May 2005 |url=https://www.theguardian.com/business/2005/may/12/7 |access-date=2022-01-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211107175507/https://www.theguardian.com/business/2005/may/12/7 |archive-date=2021-11-07 |url-status=live}} ==Acquisitions== Early acquisitions of stores included 209 stores with the acquisition of First Sport from [[Blacks Outdoor Retail|Blacks Leisure Group]] in December 2001{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=hkXgv54qSgUC&pg=PA375|title=The Marketing of Sport|page=375|first1=John |last1=Beech |first2=Simon |last2=Chadwick|publisher=Financial Times International|year=2006|isbn=978-0-273-68826-6}} and 70 stores from the administrators of Allsports in October 2005. [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]] were placed under investigation by the [[Competition and Markets Authority]] (CMA) due to alleged breaches in competition law in September 2021. The investigation was in regard to anti-competitive agreements over the sale of club branded merchandise in the UK. September 2021|work=City AM|access-date=1 October 2021}} ===Covert meetings between the Chief Executive Officers of JD Sports and Footasylum=== After the company acquired [[Footasylum]] in March 2019, the CMA carried out an investigation and then, on the basis that the company's ownership of Footasylum might limit competition, ordered the company to dispose of Footasylum.{{cite news|url=https://www.retailgazette.co.uk/blog/2021/12/jd-sports-close-to-losing-ownership-of-footasylum/|title=JD Sports close to losing ownership of Footasylum|date=13 December 2021|newspaper=Retail Gazette|access-date=15 February 2022}} The company and, its subsidiary, Footasylum, were fined a combined £4.7 million after the CEO of JD Sports, Peter Cowgill, allegedly met covertly with the CEO of Footasylum, Barry Bown, on two occasions in July and August 2021 in breach of an order from the CMA not to exchange commercially sensitive information without CMA consent. One of the meetings was alleged to have taken place in a car park in [[Bury, Greater Manchester]].{{cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/business/retail-consumer/britain-fines-jd-sports-footasylum-64-mln-breaching-order-2022-02-14/|title=Britain fines JD Sports, Footasylum as CEO meetings breach order|date=14 February 2022|newspaper=Reuters| access-date=15 February 2022}}{{cite news|url=https://news.sky.com/story/jd-sports-and-footasylum-fined-4-7m-for-secret-meetings-12541924|title=JD Sports and Footasylum fined £4.7m for secret meetings|date=14 February 2022|newspaper=Sky News| access-date=15 February 2022}}{{cite news|url=https://www.retailgazette.co.uk/blog/2022/02/jd-sports-and-footasylum-fined-5m-for-breaching-cma-order-following-covert-car-park-meeting/|title=JD Sports and Footasylum fined £5m for breaching CMA order after covert car park meeting| date=14 February 2022|newspaper=Retail Gazette| access-date=15 February 2022}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== {{Commons category}} * {{official website|https://WWW.jdsports.co.uk}} {{FTSE 100 Index constituents}} {{Queens Park Rangers F.C. shirt sponsors}} {{Authority control}} [[Category:1981 establishments in England]] [[Category:Sportswear brands]] [[Category:Clothing retailers of England]] [[Category:Clothing companies of England]] [[Category:Retail companies established in 1981]] [[Category:Companies based in Bury, Greater Manchester]] [[Category:British companies established in 1981]] [[Category:Sporting goods retailers of the United Kingdom]] [[Category:Companies listed on the London Stock Exchange]] [[Category:English brands]] [[Category:1996 initial public offerings]] [[Category:Companies in the FTSE 100 Index]]
extract: JD Sports Fashion plc, commonly known as JD Sports, JD or JD Group is a British multinational sports-fashion retail company based in Bury, Greater Manchester, England. It is listed on the London Stock Exchange and is a constituent of the FTSE 100 Index. The Pentland Group owns 55% of the company.  The company operates mainly in Europe, North America and Asia-Pacific.
